blocks.text: Grey Glacier: the ice front below cloud-covered mountains

Transfer to the airport for your flight to Santiago. On arrival, take a sightseeing tour with an English-speaking guide.

The route starts in the city centre at La Moneda Palace. Built in 1799, in the final years of Spanish rule, the neoclassical building originally housed the royal mint. It has served as the seat of the Chilean government since the mid-19th century.

Next, visit Plaza de Armas, Santiago’s main square. It is home to historic government buildings, the Central Post Office, the former Royal Audiencia and the Metropolitan Cathedral.

The next stop is Santa Lucía Hill for a panoramic view of the city. The tour continues through the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia, along the Mapocho River and Santiago’s main avenues.

On Rapa Nui, archaeological sites are spread across the island, with each day focused on a different theme. Ahu Akivi introduces you to the restored statues and the quarry at Puna Pau. At Orongo, you learn about the Birdman cult, while Rano Raraku and Tongariki showcase the largest concentration of moai. The visit to Anakena rounds off several days among volcanic slopes and ceremonial platforms with beach time by the ocean.

Santiago: glass towers against a backdrop of snowy mountains
Santiago to Easter Island and Ahu Akivi

Fly from Santiago to Easter Island. On arrival, begin your excursion to Ahu Akivi.

There are seven restored moai here. According to legend, they depict seven explorers sent to Rapa Nui by King Hotu Matu’a. Then visit Ahu Hanga Poukura, an unrestored platform.

Next is Puna Pau, where red volcanic tuff was quarried from the slope of an extinct volcano to make the headdresses for the stone statues.

Then visit the Tahai ceremonial complex. It has three main platforms with moai: Ko Te Riku, whose statue has restored eyes, Tahai and Vai Uri. The complex is part of Rapa Nui National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
